newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks improving, propane prices up - EIA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks improving, propane prices up - EIA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas stocks have increased in the last two weeks in comparison with last year's levels, the chief of the Energy Information Administration said Wednesday.
EIA Administrator Jay Hakes also said propane prices reached $1.31 per gallon last week according to the last EIA weekly price survey.
"Gas stocks are in better shape than a couple of weeks ago relative to last year's levels," Hakes said at a briefing on the EIA's long-term energy outlook.
Hakes said gas inventories were 8 percent below year-ago levels, compared with 10 percent below year-ago levels two weeks ago.
The EIA's most recent price survey showed propane prices last week reached $1.31 per gallon, 6 cents higher than the previous week and 40 cents higher than last year, he said.
Propane stocks were never fully replenished after last winter's unusually severe cold, and demand for propane was strong for drying crops, resulting in tight supplies, he said.
Distillate inventories were about 10 percent below last year's levels, Hakes said, adding that inventory levels for most products were "stable or improving."

Hakes said natural gas and propane supplies appeared adequate for the winter. "The issue here is price, as far as I'm concerned," he said, adding that those markets will be strongly influenced by the weather.
